verification.fact_verification_explanation: The central allegation is that the 60-days-past-due credit report entry is wrong because the customer never missed a payment in 18 months. The records contradict this. The 2026-03-18 and 2026-04-18 scheduled installments of $140.00 each were not received, and the log shows no payments on those dates. On 2026-04-20 the account was reported to the bureaus as 60 days past due. The customer then paid $280.00 on 2026-05-18, covering two installments, and the 2026-06-18 installment was received, so the account is now current. The reported delinquency did happen, and the missed payments are the cause. The customer's statements that every payment was on time and that the report is therefore wrong are not supported. Only the 2026-01-18 and 2026-02-18 payments are in the window shown, so the claim about the earlier 18 months was not tested, but this does not affect the outcome. Note for the reviewer: on 2026-04-20 the oldest unpaid installment (2026-03-18) was about 33 days old, while two installments were unpaid. Confirm how the '60 days past due' status was calculated before the response characterizes the reporting as accurate, and confirm whether the bureau tradeline has been updated now that the account is current.
verification.risk_rationale: No attorney/regulator reference, identity-theft dispute, embedded instructions, UDAAP-pattern or collector-conduct allegation, hardship, or vulnerability is present, and the claim is confirmed false against clear payment records on a routine credit-reporting dispute with small installment amounts ($140 each).

policy.text:
# Policy: Credit Reporting Disputes (Fair Credit Reporting Act)

**Applies to:** Any complaint alleging inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable information reported to a consumer reporting agency (credit bureau).

## Requirements
- As a furnisher of information, we must investigate a dispute (received either directly from the consumer or relayed by a credit bureau) within **30 days**, extendable to **45 days** if the consumer provides additional information during the 30-day window.
- We must review all relevant information provided by the consumer, correct any inaccuracy found, and report the results of the investigation back to the consumer and, if applicable, to the credit bureau.
- If an item is found to be inaccurate or unverifiable, it must be corrected or deleted from our reporting **promptly**.
- We may not resume reporting an item we previously deleted unless we can certify the information is accurate and complete.
- A consumer may request a statement of the dispute to be included in their credit file if the dispute is not resolved to their satisfaction.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May confirm whether our internal records match or contradict what is reported (e.g., payment history, account status).
- May state the applicable 30/45-day investigation timeline.
- May NOT promise a specific bureau will update within a specific number of days — we control our own furnishing, not the bureau's processing timeline.

## Escalation trigger
A **third or subsequent dispute on the same item**, or any complaint stating an investigation was closed with no explanation of what was actually checked, should be escalated — repeated unresolved disputes carry elevated regulatory risk.

## Remedy authority
Front-line staff may initiate a correction to our own furnished data (status, balance, payment history) when the internal transaction record clearly supports the correction. Removing an account entirely, or correcting identity-mismatch issues, requires supervisor or fraud-team review.

*Source: Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1681 et seq. Generic, illustrative summary for internal training/demo purposes, not legal advice.*

draft.draft_text:
You contacted us because your account is showing as 60 days past due on your credit report, and you believe every payment over the past 18 months was made on time. We reviewed your payment history.

Here is what we found for each point you raised:

1. Account showing 60 days past due: Our records show that the $140.00 installments due on March 18, 2026 and April 18, 2026 were not received. On April 20, 2026, the account was reported as 60 days past due. We received a $280.00 payment on May 18, 2026, covering both installments, and the June 18, 2026 installment was also received. Your account is now current. We are also reviewing how the "60 days past due" status was calculated on April 20, 2026, and whether the information we report needs to be corrected.

2. Never missed a payment: Our records do not show payments on March 18 or April 18, 2026, so we cannot confirm this part of your statement.

3. Bank statements showing on-time payments: We have not seen these statements. If they show payments on or around March 18 or April 18, 2026 that we have not recorded, please reply with copies so we can include them in our review.

No change to your credit reporting has been made at this time. We will complete our review within 30 days. If you send additional information during that period, the review may take up to 45 days. We will tell you the results, and we will correct any information we report if our review finds it is inaccurate. We cannot control when a credit bureau updates its records. If you are not satisfied with the outcome, you may ask to have a statement of your dispute added to your credit file. You are also free to contact any other agency or advisor about this matter.

To follow up, reply to this message or call the number on your account and give us your case reference: 23623033.

verifier.groundedness_check: fail — "No change to your credit reporting has been made at this time." The verification output does not establish this. It tells the reviewer to confirm whether the bureau tradeline has been updated now that the account is current, so the status is unknown. Also weakly supported: "We have not seen these statements," since nothing in the verification confirms whether the customer submitted them. "We are also reviewing how the '60 days past due' status was calculated" turns an internal reviewer note into a commitment to the customer.
verifier.tone_structure_check: fail — The outcome and next-steps content is packed into one dense paragraph of about 8 sentences, against Policy 11's 2–4 sentence limit. It mixes the review status, timeline, bureau caveat, dispute-statement option and the 'free to contact other agencies' line. The customer's action item (send bank statements) sits inside finding #3 instead of a distinct next-steps section. Finding #1 also runs to 4 sentences and combines facts with a new commitment.
specific_issues: Groundedness: the claim that no change has been made to credit reporting is unsupported, because the tradeline update status is unconfirmed in the verification output. The statement about not having seen the bank statements and the 'we are reviewing the calculation' commitment also lack clear support.

Tone/structure: the outcome and next-steps paragraph is far too long and blends several topics, violating Policy 11's short-paragraph and separated-section guidance. The customer's required action is buried in the findings section.

Completeness, policy authorization and prohibited language checks passed: all three allegations are addressed, no remedy is stated, and no fault admissions, future guarantees, legal conclusions or discouragement of other channels were found.

draft.draft_text:
You contacted us because your account is showing as 60 days past due on your credit report, and you told us you have made every payment on time. We take that seriously, and here is what we found.

What we found:

1. Reported 60 days past due: Our records show the account was reported to the credit bureaus as 60 days past due on April 20, 2026.

2. Never missed a payment: Our payment records do not show receipt of your $140.00 installments due March 18, 2026 and April 18, 2026. We received $280.00 on May 18, 2026, which covered two installments, and we received the June 18, 2026 installment. Our records show your account is now current.

3. Bank statements show on-time payments for 18 months: Our review looked at the recent payment history, January through June 2026. We have not reviewed earlier months. Based on that history, our records do not match your statement that every payment was made on time.

Outcome: We have not made any correction to the information we report, because our records do not currently support one. We have not approved or promised any other remedy.

Next steps: If your bank statements show payments of $140.00 leaving your account on or around March 18 and April 18, 2026, please reply with copies. We will review them as part of our investigation. Credit reporting disputes are investigated within 30 days, which can extend to 45 days if you send additional information. We cannot say when a credit bureau will update its records, because the bureaus control their own processing.

If you are not satisfied with the result, you may ask to have a statement of your dispute included in your credit file. You are also free to contact any other agency or advisor about this matter.

Case reference: 23623033

The verification output explicitly flags an unresolved discrepancy: on 2026-04-20 the oldest unpaid installment (2026-03-18) was only about 33 days old, so the '60 days past due' status may have been miscalculated. The reviewer note says to confirm how the status was calculated before the response characterizes the reporting as accurate, and to confirm whether the bureau tradeline has been updated now that the account is current. The draft implicitly treats the reporting as supported and gives no sign that either point was checked. The missed payments are grounded, but the conclusion that no correction is supported is not.
specific_issues: Groundedness: the 'no correction because records do not support one' outcome is not supported, because the verification output leaves open whether the '60 days past due' status was calculated correctly (oldest unpaid installment about 33 days old on the report date). The draft also does not address whether the tradeline reflects the account being current. The cited policy requires correcting any inaccuracy found, so this should be resolved, or the draft should be held for human review, before sending.
